```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_knit$set(root.dir=normalizePath('..'))
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo=TRUE,warning=TRUE,message=FALSE,fig.width=10,fig.height=5)
```

```{r import}
source('R/core.R')
input <- read.csv(params$csv,check.names=FALSE,stringsAsFactors=FALSE,na.strings=c('','NA'))
clean <- clean_prices(input)
analysis <- analyse_prices(clean$rows,as.integer(params$rolling_window))
tail_analysis <- analyse_stress(analysis$returns)
p <- clean$rows
```

## Data and provenance

Loaded file: **`r params$csv`**. Retained **`r nrow(p)`** common price observations from **`r p$date[1]`** to **`r tail(p$date,1)`**. Dropped **`r clean$quality$droppedRows`** incomplete dates.

The bundled `examples/prices.csv` is a small **synthetic calculation fixture**, not market history. For historical analysis, run `R/refresh_data.R` first and set `csv` to `analysis-output/prices.csv`. Check the accompanying metadata for the source and actual coverage.

No forward-fill, interpolation, winsorisation or annualisation is applied. Date alignment alone does not synchronise market closes. Gold futures are not physical gold; DXY is not an investment portfolio.

## Computed statistics

```{r stats}
statistics <- do.call(rbind,lapply(assets,function(k) data.frame(
  Asset=k,TotalChange=analysis$stats[[k]]$totalReturn,
  IntervalVolatility=analysis$stats[[k]]$intervalVolatility,
  MaxDrawdown=analysis$stats[[k]]$maxDrawdown)))
knitr::kable(statistics,digits=5)
```

Volatility is the sample standard deviation of log returns between consecutive common observations. It is not annualised or labelled as a fixed 24-hour return.

## Normalised price performance

```{r performance}
normalised <- as.matrix(p[assets])
normalised <- sweep(normalised,2,normalised[1,],'/')*100
matplot(as.Date(p$date),normalised,type='l',lty=1,log='y',col=c('#c4784b','#b6a06b','#6a87a7'),xlab='Date',ylab='Price index, base 100',main='Normalised price observations')
legend('topleft',legend=assets,col=c('#c4784b','#b6a06b','#6a87a7'),lty=1,bty='n')
```

## Log-return correlation

```{r correlation}
correlations <- do.call(rbind,lapply(analysis$matrix,unlist))
knitr::kable(correlations,digits=4)
```

Undefined correlations remain missing when a series has zero variance. No fixed result or hedge label is printed.

## Trailing Bitcoin / Gold correlation

```{r rolling}
r <- analysis$rolling
if(nrow(r)>0 && any(is.finite(r$bitcoin_gold))) {
  plot(as.Date(r$date),r$bitcoin_gold,type='l',ylim=c(-1,1),col='#c4784b',xlab='Window ending',ylab='Pearson correlation',main=paste(params$rolling_window,'common-observation window'))
  abline(h=0,lty=2,col='grey')
} else cat('Insufficient observations or zero variance for a defined rolling estimate.')
```

## Conditional dollar-tail analysis

The upper-decile DXY-return cutoff is **`r signif(tail_analysis$threshold,5)`**, with **`r tail_analysis$n`** strictly positive DXY-return intervals selected. This cutoff is estimated in-sample.

```{r stress}
knitr::kable(do.call(rbind,lapply(assets,function(k) data.frame(
  Asset=k,MeanAll=tail_analysis$baseline[[k]]$meanLogReturn,
  MeanTail=tail_analysis$conditional[[k]]$meanLogReturn,
  NegativeShareTail=tail_analysis$conditional[[k]]$negativeShare))),digits=5)
```

This descriptive subset is not a causal estimate or a safe-haven classification. DCC-GARCH, Markov-switching, ETF-flow analysis and predictive models remain outside this implementation.
